summary: ethereum-vault-connector exfiltrates installer secrets to webhook.site on install
details: Package impersonates Euler's Ethereum Vault Connector. Both preinstall and postinstall lifecycle hooks execute index.js, which enumerates process.env for credential-shaped keys (matching KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|PRIVATE|MNEMONIC|RPC|AWS|GITHUB|NPM|KUBE|VAULT|AUTH|PGP|GPG|SEED|WALLET), reads ~/.npmrc and ~/.gitconfig, lists ~/.ssh, ~/.foundry/keystores, ~/.config/hardhat, and ~/.config/gcloud, and collects hostname, username, cwd, and platform/arch via os.hostname()/os.userInfo()/os.platform(). The collected JSON is POSTed via https.request to a hardcoded webhook.site collector at path /326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09. A file-header comment falsely presents the script as a '@plumenetwork/nest-artifacts install-time shim' for toolchain validation; errors are swallowed via `|| true` and try/catch to hide failures during install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
